you want a visually breathtaking open world to explore
you enjoy cooperative multiplayer modes alongside the campaign

you cannot stand unskippable cutscenes and dialogue sequences

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as fluid and satisfying, featuring smooth swordplay and precise parries.

citations.review_text: Ghost of Tsushima is an absolute masterpiece. Visually, the game is stunning, with breathtaking landscapes of swaying pampas grass and vibrant autumn leaves that make every frame look like a painting. Its story is deeply moving, tracking Jin Sakai’s emotional transition from an honorable samurai to a ruthless shadow warrior. Combined with incredibly fluid, satisfying sword combat and an immersive guiding wind system, it delivers an unforgettable experience that perfectly captures the soul of classic samurai cinema.
prettiest game i ever did play, solid story, really beautiful open world, combat is some of the best i played too

Excellent. 10/10. The combat system is very enjoyable with smooth movements and accurate response times. Story is great with engaging and believable character arcs. World is beautiful with authentic feudal Japan feeling. Exploration is rewarded with upgrades to stats, weapons, and cosmetics. Definitely appropriate for casual gaming with fast travels throughout, anytime saves, and adjustable difficulty levels. If you want a more grounded and less fantasy/mythological experience then this is the game for you.

👍 Recommended

Ghost of Tsushima is one of those games that completely pulled me into its world. The island is beautiful, the atmosphere is incredible, and the wind-guided exploration is one of the best navigation systems I've seen in an open-world game.

The combat is easily my favorite part. Every duel feels intense, and landing perfect parries or finishing enemies with clean sword strikes never gets old. Combined with the amazing soundtrack and visuals, the game constantly makes you feel like you're playing through a samurai movie.

It's not perfect, though. Some side activities and enemy camps can become repetitive, especially if you're aiming for 100% completion. A few missions also feel a bit stretched out. But honestly, those issues never stopped me from enjoying the game.

What really makes Ghost of Tsushima special is how everything comes together—the story, the combat, the world, and the atmosphere. Jin's journey is memorable, and by the end I was far more invested than I expected.

A great game with a few flaws, but one I'll happily remember for a long time.

9.5/10 — I'd follow foxes across the entire island again. 🦊⚔️

With all the hype it had and all the positives I have heard about its accuracy and all that I was quite interested to play the game myself. I have seen the honor related dialogues and stuff and even without knowing the context I was kinda sold about it. Although several aspects are very well designed, the game feels so generic in the end.
Good Stuff:
There wont be much in here but would be unfair not to mention. Some of these also have a counterpart in negatives
- GPS:
The wind showing you directions is probably the most stylish and best looking mechanic of showing the player directions I have seen in a game so far. It is a detail that adds to the whole ezoteric wind is by my side lone samurai vibe and whoever made that up is the MVP.
- Difficulty:
The lethal difficulty makes the combat so satisfying (at first). You are pretty much one shot from dying to anything and you have to actually outskill multiple opponents. So once you do, youdo feel like a legendary samurai of a myth.
- Romantic look on the era:
All the birds leading you to points of interest, the foxes doing the same, the bamboo slicing stands and the almost fairytale looking locations really spot on hit the vibe the game was intended to have.
Bad stuff:
- Combat:
While I praised the lethal difficulty, I still dislike the fact that there is just a handful of enemy types with the same movesets and these movesets are not large. So at first you might feel overwhelmed by a group of enemies but later in the game you are like "Two axe guys, two bow guys and one spear guy" and do the "satisfying" dance of getting them all in one big successin of counterattacks. This does not change throughout the whole game and in arc 1 you pretty much experience all combat has to offer.
- Writing:
Even though I was quite disappointed to see what the game is after hearing how accurate and faithful it is, I wont hold the inaccuracies against the game. Samurai werent really the honorable protectors of the common folk,…

citations.review_text:
I’m only a few hours in, but honestly, every session so far has felt borderline insufferable. It has that very polished, cinematic Sony game feel, but underneath all the presentation, I’m struggling to find anything I actually enjoy.

These ♥♥♥♥ ass controls actually feel like they were designed by a literal toddler. Everything feels unnecessarily awkward and outdated, and I’m constantly fighting the controls instead of actually enjoying the game.

The dialogue is also hella corny. A lot of the conversations feel overly serious and forced, and I find myself wanting to skip through them rather than actually caring about what anyone is saying. Unfortunately, you cannot even do that. 

Movement feels painfully slow too, and the horse somehow manages to make it worse. It makes me want to just go straight from objective to objective rather than exploring the world. 

Maybe it gets better later, but based on my first few hours, this is just more Sony slop wrapped in a pretty package. I’ve already reached the point where starting another session feels like a chore rather than something I’m looking forward to.

I can’t really give it a score out of 10 but so far things aren’t looking good. I’m sure I will come round the finishing the game at some point but for now this one can wait. 

By the looks of things, Playstation should have gate kept this game like they do with all the others and let it die with their console.

citations.review_text:
A lot has been said about how beautiful this game is and combat is really fluid no doubt, so no point repeating, but i just wanna say how terrible the side story missions are in this game, with no thought put whatsoever.  
The world feels super dead, where either you are climbing or petting fox which irritates after few times or no matter the mission going killing mongols coming back, Repeat.
Typical sony slop and boy they really love adding climbing in games be it this one or god of war or uncharted.

amazing story. amazing plot. sidequests are maybe slightly repetitive but the overall structure and feel of the game oversides that part. the emotional parts of the game is something i felt gives the game more life. 10/10 and recommends to everyone to play this masterpiece before u die

will recommend to anyone. combat is very simple but very fun. its very nutty and flowing with multiple enamines and parring in this game is very rewarding. unlocking ability's is simple but not respective with some requiring a quest to unlock some you unlock via the skill tree. the story is very convincing and well written. side content is ok it depends on the person but near the end of the game it felt reparative, that's my only complaint.

So where do I even start with this one...

This is not a bad game. In terms of visuals and art direction, it’s honestly beautiful. The art team absolutely carried this game. The world looks amazing, the atmosphere is incredible, and every location feels like someone spent a lot of time making it look perfect.

So yeah... points for coloring inside the lines.

And that's where my biggest praise ends.

The first few hours are actually really entertaining, but after that the game becomes extremely repetitive. Exploration is probably my biggest disappointment. The game constantly tells you where everything is, and when you finally go there, the reward is usually dung or a pebble-tier item that you’ll never care about.

Exploration should make you curious. Here, it feels more like checking boxes on a map.

The pacing also killed the experience for me. I swear around 40% of my playtime was just watching unskippable dialogue, 30% was riding from one point to another, and the rest was the actual gameplay.

And the difficulty? Honestly, this game is not challenging at all. It feels like it holds your hand from beginning to end. The combat looks stylish, but the game rarely pushes you to actually master it.

The skill points you get also feel mostly useless because I never felt any real need to change stances. You can basically pick whatever you like, stick with it, and you’ll finish the game just fine. The systems are there, but the game never really forces you to engage with them.

Even the final fights (both the main game and DLC) were disappointing. After everything leading up to them, I expected something more memorable, but they ended up feeling underwhelming.

I’m still going to finish the online mode because that actually looks more interesting. Having different classes and a more focused gameplay loop sounds like it might fit the game better than the main story.

Overall, is a beautiful game with incredible presentation, but underneath all that …

Ghost of Tsushima is one of the best open-world games I have played in recent years.
The gameplay is fantastic and highly varied. Every enemy type requires a different approach, which keeps combat engaging throughout the entire game. The sound of the swords, the parry and deflect mechanics, and the overall flow of combat feel incredibly satisfying and well-balanced. In many ways, it reminded me of Sekiro, where timing and skill are heavily rewarded.
The world itself is absolutely stunning. Exploring the island of Tsushima is a joy, with breathtaking landscapes, beautiful environments, and plenty of reasons to wander off the main path. I also enjoyed the side stories of the island's inhabitants, which helped bring the world to life.
That said, some side missions felt repetitive and occasionally reminded me of the typical Ubisoft formula. Fortunately, the Mythic Tales more than make up for it. They are easily some of the best content in the game, featuring memorable stories, unique rewards, and excellent presentation.
The main story is well-written, emotional, and compelling, although it does suffer from some pacing issues and unnecessary stretching at times.
Overall, Ghost of Tsushima delivers an incredible samurai experience with outstanding combat, a gorgeous open world, and a strong story. It's a game I would highly recommend to anyone who enjoys action-adventure games.
Score: 9/10

claims.claim: The game features a navigation system that uses guiding wind and natural visual cues rather than a cluttered HUD or traditional map markers.

citations.review_text: You play as Jin Sakai, a samurai forced to break his strict moral code to save his people from a brutal invasion. The world is jaw-droppingly beautiful, letting you ditch messy menus and explore naturally by just following the wind, foxes, and birds. Combat feels incredible, switching seamlessly from intense, respectful sword duels to silent assassin takedowns. It is a deeply moving story about sacrifice that leaves a lasting impression long after the credits roll.

Really loving the open world system in here! There are enough contextual clues hidden for you to track and discover within the world, so much so that you might not need to open map constantly. Plus the character levelling is very different, where the majority of the levelling can be done within Act 1 itself, and the other Acts just let you utilise the all the tools you have earned. There's no consistent checklist, no cluttered HUD, and the story so far has been pretty engaging. It felt a bit cookie cutter in the start, but the as it progressed-along with the side characters-it has dug its hook pretty deep. The samurai feels are right there to immerse in. So far an awesome job!!

[h1]First Impressions: The World of Tsushima[/h1]
The island of Tsushima carries generations of history and secrets, serving as home to samurai, peasants, ronin, and ruthless bandits alike. Riding through its landscapes feels remarkably serene, offering quiet moments to process the heavy narrative while witnessing how such breathtaking natural beauty coexists with widespread tragedy. Every charred village and swaying field of pampa grass tells an implicit story of the Mongol invasion, inviting you to imagine the horrors that unfolded before your arrival. Tsushima shines by refusing to overwhelm the player with map clutter or intrusive quest markers, choosing instead to guide your journey organically through the Guiding Wind and natural visual cues.

[h1]The Jin Sakai Story & Character Progression[/h1]
Jin Sakai begins his journey as a brave and dedicated samurai following in the footsteps of his late father, the formidable leader of Clan Sakai. As the Mongol invasion devastates Tsushima, Jin realizes that clinging blindly to samurai tradition will only lead to total defeat. To protect his people, he is forced to prioritize survival over protocol, ultimately embarking on the darker path of the Ghost. His transformation is driven by brutal necessity. The Mongol commander, Khotun Khan, spent years studying samurai tactics, using their rigid code of honor to easily predict and dismantle their defenses. This creates a compelling ideological rift between Lord Shimura and the thief Yuna. Shimura remains an idealist, convinced that victory without honor is meaningless, even if it leads to slaughter. Yuna exposes the grim reality on the ground: if the samurai do not adapt, Tsushima will burn. Unbound by rigid rules, the Ghost becomes an unpredictable, terrifying force to the invaders, while inspiring the desperate populace to view Jin as their savior. For Jin, however, this evolution comes at an immense personal cost. Divided between devotion to his uncle and his duty to…

TL:DR - A great game at the likes of games such as RDR2 in terms of characters, storytelling and its open world. Recommend you play on hard difficulty. Buy it, especially on sale, well worth the money. Only real drawback is playstation/sony is the publisher.

+ An interesting storyline with additional optional but equally interesting side stories.
+ An open world split into 4 regions, each with slight to greatly different biomes as well as increased enemy difficulty and variance.
+ Fun combat where you can choose your playstyle after the many weapon choices, though you will generally let the katana do the heavy lifting during the game.
+ You'll meet a great many all around well made characters, with only rarely being puzzled by the choices they make (looking at masako adachi).
+ Exploration is recommended though still optional where you'll often find anything from weapon skins, small health buffs, item buffs or resources to help upgrade armor and weapons.
+ UI is one of the best out there as its formed to be as minimal and unintrusive as possible. Even the map location tool is the actual wind guiding you.
+ Scenery is gorgeous and the game even has its built in screenshot function where you can adjust things like time of day, weather, and the like.
+ Fast travel that lives up to the name. Unlike a lot of games where a 8+ second loading screen will pop up, the fast travel here takes 2 seconds.
+ Options for English voice acting, Japanese, and even a black and white graphical playthrough.
+/- Not really any puzzles in game, closest would be certain shrines on Iki island.
+/- Some of the character side quests can be a bit long cause sometimes there's not much happening in each quest segment, but at least you get to know the characters more and more.
---- Sony being sony, they're kinda pushy and weird about you making an account. Hiding skins but also certain gameplay content behind it.

Ghost of Tsushima is honestly everything I ever wanted from a samurai game.

The world is so breathtaking it almost feels alive. I constantly find myself just standing still, listening to the soft rustle of the pampas grass and watching crimson maple leaves swirl around Jin. And that guiding wind? Pure magic. It is such a poetic, beautiful way to explore without a clunky HUD ruining the view.

The game is a massive love letter to classic Akira Kurosawa films, making you feel like you are actively playing through a masterpiece like Seven Samurai or Yojimbo. The combat feels incredibly powerful and precise, where every single clash of steel looks and sounds like a cinematic movie scene. The story hits all the right notes, capturing that heavy spirit of honour, loyalty, and sacrifice perfectly. Jin Sakai is written so well as a warrior torn between rigid tradition and raw survival, and watching his internal struggle unfold during those tense, cinematic duels is just gripping.

The only reason it isn't completely flawless is that a few side missions can get a bit repetitive. But honestly? It is easily one of the greatest gaming experiences out there.

citations.review_text:
[b]Ghost of Tsushima[/b] just feels good to play. 

There are some moments when it reminds me of [i]The Witcher 3[/i] and [i]Red Dead Redemption 2[/i]. Still, [i]Ghost of Tsushima[/i] has its own rhythm. People like to compare it with [i]Assassin's Creed[/i], but I never really saw it that way. The world is less of a checklist, the progression is more rewarding, and every new skill brings Jin Sakai closer to actually becoming the [b]Ghost[/b].

The sword has weight. Hits feel sharp. Executions feel vicious. Blood actually adds to the impact instead of just decorating the screen. It is brutal, satisfying and ridiculously well put together.

It is also a beautiful Kurosawa tribute without constantly screaming about it.

[b]You need some patience.[/b] The game can be slow, dialogues and cinematics cannot be skipped on your first playthrough, and the wind-guiding system takes a little while to get used to. Once you do, it becomes part of the world. Give it a chance.

Do not ask me why [i]The Witcher 3[/i] could not pull me in and this one did.

It just did.

What the actual f-ck is this game? I've never felt so emotionally dismembered by a computer game. This is absolute perfection, and hats off to the designer who pushed through with the "we do not allow cut scenes to be skipped" concept. This game is truly magnificent. loved every minute of it, laughed, cried, got emotionally dismembered, chewed on and spat out, but would do it over and again regardless. Amazing voice actors, incredible story, greatest combat controls and mechanics ever. LOVE it
amazing game with a great story and combat. my only complaint is that some dialogues can't be skipped..

claims.claim: Combat mechanics allow players to switch between sword stances, parries, dodges, and stealth takedowns.

citations.review_text: You play as Jin Sakai, a samurai forced to break his strict moral code to save his people from a brutal invasion. The world is jaw-droppingly beautiful, letting you ditch messy menus and explore naturally by just following the wind, foxes, and birds. Combat feels incredible, switching seamlessly from intense, respectful sword duels to silent assassin takedowns. It is a deeply moving story about sacrifice that leaves a lasting impression long after the credits roll.

Played through Tsushima again before I went through Yotei, and still think this is one of the best singleplayer experiences I've ever played. The story is incredibly gripping, weaving the historical events on Tsushima island perfectly while giving the writers enough freedom to create an incredible protagonist in Jin Sakai.
His evolution from the honor bound bushido samurai to shinobi, sacrificing everything he has to save his people is incredibly well written.
The raw gameplay is one of the best ive seen, even though it keeps it relatively simple (light/heavy/charge attacks + parry/dodge counterattack system) it's incredibly satisfying to go through encounters on Lethal without taking a single hit.
As someone who has played both, I still think in terms of writing and straight combat Tsushima does a better job, particularly in comparing lethal difficulty in both games (which i would recommend doing in Tsushima but not Yotei)

Overall I still absolutely recommend this game to anyone interested in singleplayer games, even if samurai isnt something you're interested in.

Played this with high expectations, was not disappointed.
It's one of those games where everything is well done and curated;
The world is beautiful, with little details here and there that make it feel "alive", make it tell those stories that give a third dimension to it.
The story is narrated incredibly weel, it makes you get attached to the characters, to their stories, to what is happening in Tsushima.
Exploring the island never feels like a chore thanks to how the game rewards curiosity, with both side stories scattered all over, collectibles, or views that are so breath taking to be worth screencapping (and eventually even using as backgrounds).

The combat system is also wonderful. Easy to pick up but with enough layers to it to keep engaging. The stances, parry + dodge mechanics, the ghost weapons and all the rest, with enemies growing stronger and deadlier as you progress make combat evolve with you.

This game isn't trying to invent anything new. It's things that already exist, but it's just shaping them in the perfect way.

It's one of the best open world games I've ever played and absolutely worth playing.

citations.review_text: This game is a total slog. Just another Sony story book game. The combat was fun, but there was far too much "start mission, go on horseback walk side by side (done better in rdr1/2). Or start mission and "investigate the area for more clues". It's the most paint by numbers trash for the tourists of gaming, this same stuff happens in days gone. I Uninstalled multiple times but kept coming back over the course of a year to enjoy some mindless combat and I Uninstalled it as soon as the credits started rolling (maybe i beat it out of sunk Cost fallacy). It's a good port, it runs great maxed out at native 1440p, but thats about where the good stuff ends.

Ghost of Tsushima is a phenomenal open world action adventure game set during the Mongol invasion of Japan on the Tsushima island. The game follows a honorable Samurai Jin Sakai who starts to question his morality and definition of honor as brutality of war with Mongols intensifies and seeing their cruelty on his own people. His character development from a honorable samurai to a Ghost who fights from the shadow and can cross any lines to defeat the Mongols my any means necessary was an incredible character arc. Being able to play as a samurai and a ninja was a great and fun experience.
The later expansion of Iki Island was superb as well that explored the dark past of Jin's Father when they tried to subdue this island. The world of Ghost of Tsushima was incredibly beautiful the grassland to swamps to temples all them genuinely capture to beauty of Japan and its culture.
The villains such as Khotun Khan and the Eagle from Iki island expansion are incredibly written as well. All the other side characters are also incredibly written. All the main quests and side quests also have great depth and story that further gives us more lore and explore the suffering of common people during this war as well. The story is incredibly emotional that sometime took my breath away.
The gameplay is also incredible as well great swordplay and great options for ghost weapons that lets us become the assassin. Although the gameplay becomes very repetitive just like other open world games but still the beauty of the world makes up for it. 
Overall, the game is a masterpiece and anyone who loves Japanese culture and Samurai should definitely try this game. I will give this game a 9.5/10.

⚔️ One More Shrine... Then Five More Hours 🌸

Some games are fun. Some games are memorable. Ghost of Tsushima somehow manages to be both while delivering one of the most beautiful open world experiences I've ever played! From the moment you step onto the island, it's almost impossible not to get completely immersed in its breathtaking landscapes, satisfying combat, and emotional story...

The world is simply stunning! Instead of filling the map with endless distractions, exploration feels natural and rewarding. Following the wind instead of a traditional waypoint, chasing foxes to hidden shrines, composing haikus, relaxing in hot springs, and discovering forgotten temples all make the island feel alive. I found myself constantly wandering off the main path just to see what was waiting over the next hill.

The combat is absolutely phenomenal. Every sword fight feels fast, precise, and incredibly satisfying! Switching stances, perfectly timing parries, and cutting through enemies with a single clean strike never gets old. As new abilities and techniques unlock, the combat only becomes more enjoyable, giving you plenty of freedom to approach encounters however you like.

The story strikes a fantastic balance between epic and personal. The journey is filled with memorable characters, emotional moments, and difficult choices that make the conflict feel meaningful. Even the side quests are worth experiencing because they add depth to both the world and the people living in it.

Visually, this game is nothing short of spectacular! Every forest, mountain, beach, and field of flowers looks like a moving painting. Whether you're riding through golden forests at sunset or crossing snowy mountain paths during a blizzard, almost every scene feels worthy of a screenshot. The PC version on Steam makes everything even better, with excellent performance, high resolution support, ultrawide compatibility, and plenty of graphics options that let the world truly shine.

That is by far one of my favorite games of all times. Quite long post folks :)

TL;DR :
Good & intuitive gameplay, great storyline, breathtaking graphics, funny online (less players than usual), around 75h for a good session :)

-------------| GAMEPLAY |-------------
The controls are pretty intuitive, and the game does not lack of hints to let you find your way through harder times. One can either choose to follow the wind all along, or try to find every breach through the rocks !
The combat system is at first destabilizing, but you get used to it quickly. 
Not too many collectibles required to 100% the game, yet a large variety of cosmectics to match your fighting style with their specs.

-------------| STORYLINE |-------------
Without spoiling, the main story is breathtaking and at some point heart-breaking. Some decisions will make the player really decide by their own iverall conception of the situation.
Main characters are unique and well driven through the Jin's journey. The NPC even share a bit when you're interested to talking to them.
The progress through the map is interesting. However, do not let your intrusive thoughts win and decide to go to Ikki before completing the main quest (quite a bad idea).
An overall well written storyline, implying major decisions and moments filled with various IRL emotions (from anger to pity...).

-------------| DESIGN |-------------
That's purely subjective, but the graphics are really nice. You can feel every atmosphere through different periods. The attention to certain details makes the environment way more dynamic than other games.
The diffenrences between regions also prove how well the designers understood the assignement : a hard zone to get in → make it surrounded by mountains, rocks that you can not climb easily ! A peaceful spot in a devastated land → make it solemn, guarded by nature regaining its rights. A moment of pure sensation → elevate the player and create a magnificent landscape for them to sightsee.

citations.review_text:
[h1][b]The Sacrifice of Honor[/b][/h1]
[b]Ghost of Tsushima DIRECTOR'S CUT[/b] is a breathtaking story about the meaning of honor, sacrifice, and conflict. You play as Jin Sakai, a samurai facing a relentless Mongol invasion of the island of Tsushima, Japan, and during your time you will have to broaden your horizons in order to defeat the merciless enemy, but at the cost of your own decency as a follower of the way of the warrior.

Personally I always put story first in games like this, which in itself is fantastic, yet they also managed to nail the gameplay. The combat is incredibly satisfying, giving you many tools to fight with, including different weapon stances, bows, throwables, and mythic abilities that still stay grounded in reality.

The graphics look amazing, the lighting is beautiful, and you can see tiny details on people's faces that really add onto cutscenes, like flowing tears and sweat, though I have ran into an issue that I couldn't really figure out as a solution to. I would constantly run into a graphical issue in which the wind and most particles would constantly flicker, and this bug would come and go, usually either starting the second I play the game, or if it didn't start then, it usually didn't show up. Might be related to me playing on Linux, I'm not sure, if anyone knows a solution then please share it with others.

I absolutely loved this game, beat it on Lethal difficulty 100%, and I wish I could play [b]Ghost of Yotei[/b] as well, yet unfortunately the PC port for it has been canned, a real shame as I'd love to immerse myself into this world yet again. Maybe one day there will come a PC port, but for now the [b]Ghost of Tsushima[/b] will be a legendary title I'll likely return to once more.

Great Hack and Slash with a very beautiful story. The combat is what really sells this game. You can sneak, you can go at it with a bow or just straight up charge the enemy sword drawn. This is a lovely time for anyone interested in the genre.

The story is kinda generic but that doesn't make it bad, just easy to figure out. 

While not a masterpiece definitely worth the time spent. 

8 out of 10
